references.observation: The pale facade has a broad cut-out through the front shell and upper rim. Radial ribs sit over tapered supports. Dark strips and blue doors show below the eaves.
The lower aisle steps bridge the base of the viewing cutaway. The sloping rim has two raised housings. Small tile patterns distinguish the landing.
The view from above records the oval bowl, red bench rows, pale stair aisles, painted basketball boundaries, turquoise keys and tiny players.

references.attribution: Jacob Richman, photograph of the visitor guide
references.observation: The guide identifies the Tel Aviv exhibit section. Its pictorial layout does not locate this miniature precisely.
Near view from the northwest shows the pale raised rim, transverse roof fittings, the cutaway and the squared platform below the terrace railing.
View from the southwest shows the side bays, the paved edge and the strip of landscaping next to the visitor path.
View from the east shows the reverse face and the relative position of the office tower exhibit, visitor paths and wooden terrace.
View from the north shows the cutaway facing the visitor path beneath the railed wooden terrace.

map.scope: PMTiles provides the park and traced path geometry. The dated camera controls establish the exhibit platform and approach direction.

rejected2012Candidate.reason: The pale shape was a possible match in the north-up mosaic. The 2012 ground views show the flower bed west of the Azrieli pad in this area. The three nearest camera stations surround it. The location is excluded for a 2012 reconstruction.
rejected2012Candidate.scope: The views establish the path and garden bed at the archive date. The arena’s platform remains unlocated.

earlyPhotoSequence.observation: The 2003 gallery places the arena photos between the power station and Teddy Stadium photos. The backdrop includes a pale wall, a blue beam and timber rail. Photo order and the backdrop establish additional search cues without fixing an exhibit pad or a compass bearing.

adjacentVisitorPhotos.finding: The photographer shows Azrieli Towers, the arena and Dizengoff Center consecutively in the Tel Aviv section. The Dizengoff photo shows two distinct towers beside a curving miniature road. The three photos are separately framed, and cannot fix the arena pad or its bearing.

sources.observation: The reviewed images show Azrieli Towers and other park displays. None shows the cutaway together with a mapped control.
The pictorial map supports the Tel Aviv search area. The arena pad remains unidentified.
The photo group shows several paved park exhibits. The arena does not appear with a recognizable neighbor.

limitations: The 2003 facade and the later visitor photograph establish the cutaway shape and bowl. Model dimensions, exact seating, signage and small trim are estimates.
The court scales the approximate 28 m basketball length at 1:25. Other dimensions are interpreted from the photographs.
The exhibit center, orientation and current display condition are pending. The photos show the miniature’s cutaway, and the available PMTiles lack a separate footprint or exhibit point.
The overhead photo shows three dark openings in the lower seating. Their azimuths follow the painted court in the photograph. Widths and depths are estimates.

seatingEntrances.note: The overhead photo shows three dark openings in the lower seating. Their azimuths follow the painted court in the photograph. Widths and depths are estimates.

entranceWings.observation: The 2003 entrance photo shows gridded window strips, blue barred doors and low planting beds along the two wings. The model interprets the scale and spacing of these details.

cutawayFinish.observation: A slender rail joins the two sides of the upper rim above the open slot. The later overhead photograph shows inset square bands and small light centers in the landing paving. The recreated inlay spacing is approximate.

seatingFinish.observation: The overhead photograph shows short red seat backs, a narrow dark blue skirt between the lower seating and the concrete court apron, and green basket frames. The raised court has fine rectangular markings inside the sidelines and the large arcs return to the baselines. The backrest sizes, grouping and spacing of the court lines are interpreted. The photo also shows yellow stair edges and slender rails near the end recesses. The reconstructed aisle layout is approximate.
